}}'''Richard Allen Isaacson''' (born October 6, 1941)<ref name=iit>{{cite web |title=Richard A. Isaacson — IIT Faculty Biography |url=http://phys.iit.edu/~segre/iit_physics_bios/isaacson_r.html |website=phys.iit.edu |access-date=14 July 2023}}</ref>  is a retired American physicist who has been cited by 2017 Nobel Laureate [[Rainer Weiss]] as indispensable to the [[LIGO]] gravitational wave project.<ref>[[NPR Weekend Edition]]: [https://www.npr.org/2019/05/19/723326933/billion-dollar-gamble-how-a-singular-hero-helped-start-a-new-field-in-physics Billion Dollar Gamble], May 19, 2019. Retrieved 19 May, 2019</ref> Isaacson's 1967 PhD dissertation established that the theoretical gravitational waves had features similar to other known types of waves.<ref>[https://drum.lib.umd.edu/handle/1903/17447 Gravitational Radiation in the Limit of High Frequency], PhD dissertation, [[University of Maryland]], 1967. Retrieved May 19, 2019</ref> Isaacson went on to champion the LIGO project as the [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] Program Director of Gravitational Physics for decades.  Weiss and fellow Laureate [[Kip Thorne]] have honored Isaacson by endowing the [[American Physical Society]]'s  ''Richard A. Isaacson Award in Gravitational-Wave Science''<ref>[https://umdphysics.umd.edu/about-us/news/department-news/1347-new-aps-award-honors-richard-isaacson.html New APS Award Honors Richard Isaacson], University of Maryland Physics Department, March 28, 2018. Retrieved May 19, 2019</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Richard A. Isaacson Award in Gravitational-Wave Science |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/isaacson.cfm |website=www.aps.org |publisher=American Physical Society |access-date=14 July 2023 |language=en}}</ref>
